item.description: - The dashboard licence is now bought and checked through Dodo Payments, and priced in US dollars. Nothing changes about what you get or how you enter a code. No licence had been sold under the old provider, so no existing licence is affected. - The paywall no longer quotes a price before you get to the checkout page, which is the one place that can state it correctly for where you are and what you're paying with. - An outage at the licence server no longer counts against you. A server error is now treated the same as having no connection at all — your Mac stays unlocked — where before it risked reading as a refusal. - Pasting into the dashboard or Settings works. Both windows used to take a click without bringing Intention to the front, which left ⌘V going to whichever app the menu bar still belonged to — so a pasted licence code went somewhere else entirely, with nothing on screen to say so. - The dashboard and Settings no longer sit above every other app's windows. They still stay lit while you're working elsewhere, which is the whole point of them, but now you can put something in front when you want to.

- Opening at login is honest about itself now. The switch reads whether macOS has actually registered Intention rather than what it was last told, so turning Intention off in System Settings is reflected here instead of the switch going on claiming it's on. - If macOS is holding the login item pending your approval — which it does sometimes, and which the app can't clear on its own — Intention says so and offers to open the right pane of System Settings, rather than appearing to be on while never starting. - Running Intention straight from the disk image or your Downloads folder now explains why opening at login and automatic updates can't work from there, instead of both quietly failing. Dragging it to Applications fixes both, and that's what it tells you.

- Intention no longer offers you an update while it's asking what you intend to do. The update window would have opened behind the overlay, which holds the screen and keeps taking focus back — leaving you unable to answer the question or dismiss the update. A check that arrives at a bad moment now waits for the overlay to close rather than being dropped.
